placement: One instance after each recovered-clock lane_align_v2. Complete block records cross into common clock; downstream four-lane deskew and rate compensation remain separate.

layout_lsb_to_msb: block[193:0] (all bits preserved even beyond declared length)
ports.input: No backpressure. Every valid live block is accepted on a recovered-clock edge or produces sticky overflow/fault. wr_accept reports actual acceptance; it is not a request to pause the serial source. Startup/reset/fault invalidates the epoch and ignores input until coordinated restart.
ports.output: Held valid+all200bits in common domain until ready. Empty means valid0; this transaction interface does not classify an idle read-ready as physical serial underflow.

resets.assertion: por_ni low OR either-domain clean level reset request asynchronously asserts BOTH local reset synchronizers and masks public traffic. Do not reset only one FIFO pointer. External reset requests must be glitch-free reset-quality levels.
resets.release: Three local reset-release flops, then four local boot clocks; each boot-ready is synchronized through two peer-clock flops. Traffic requires local boot and peer ready. The unchanged vendor core separately propagates source/sink reset. A stopped clock cannot finish the mutual startup barrier.
resets.epoch: No local epoch counter is advertised. Reset or synchronized fault invalidates pending records/partial packets; common-clock integration must abort downstream state and reacquire the lane. Already accepted output before fault becomes visible is a valid prefix, not a guarantee of complete packet integrity.

faults.local: Alignment loss, length code>4, or valid&&!vendor_ready while running makes write fault sticky. Only genuine capacity rejection sets wr_overflow. No later writes after the failing write edge.
faults.crossing: One held fault bit crosses two common-clock flops. Reader may retire previously buffered valid prefix during synchronizer latency; then public valid/ready is masked until shared reset. No instantaneous cross-clock error indication or in-order fault-marker timing is claimed.
faults.restart: Only shared reset clears fault. Merely resuming downstream ready, seeing EIEOS or deasserting loss does not recover.

capacity.supported_depth: Power of two >=4; actual tests at4,8,32
capacity.measured_test: Read clock running, output stalled and source at4recovered cycles/record: firstDEPTH+2 records accepted; next live record faults. Pointer synchronization can conservatively refuse a write before a simultaneous remote read becomes visible.
capacity.budget: DEPTH32 is a finite prototype budget, not a protocol worst-case sizing claim. For an initial occupancy Q, a pause of S common cycles and a conservative synchronization allowance L, require Q + ceil(32*ceil((S+L)*f_wr/f_rd)/66) +1 <=DEPTH for minimum66bit blocks, without relying on two prefetch entries. Actual clock tolerance/SSC, maximum pause/skew and legal compensation opportunities must be bound before full PCS sizing. An arbitrary downstream stall or long-term input excess cannot be solved by a finite FIFO.

vendor_reuse.selected: Existing Ethernet copy avoids compiling a second same-named axis_async_fifo from verilog-axis. Vendor bytes unmodified; MIT notice retained.
vendor_reuse.configuration: DATA_WIDTH200, KEEP/LAST/ID/DEST/USER/FRAME/DROP/MARK/PAUSE disabled, KEEP_WIDTH1, RAM_PIPELINE1, OUTPUT_FIFO0. Do not reuse synchronous aer_fifo for this seam.
vendor_reuse.hazard_closed: Vendor normal-mode s_ready deassertion does not itself provide the required no-backpressure overrun event. Wrapper explicitly latches rejected live blocks.

next_component: Four common-clock per-lane queues and bounded deskew acquisition keyed to a declared training/alignment episode. Must disambiguate repeated identical EIEOS, enforce lane mapping and bound skew; do not match arbitrary first markers or equate CDC success with deskew. SKP scheduling, insertion/deletion and trailer LFSR policy are separate.

primary_reference.findings: SerDes RxData arrives with recovered RxCLK; RxValid indicates clock stability. The original-PIPE elastic-buffer compensation/reset rules are a different interface contract. This new block is an internal MAC CDC seam, not an implementation claim for original-PIPE status/reset timing.
primary_reference.distribution: Internal PDF/text are not included in any public capsule; only official link and exact file hashes.

validation.clock_conditions: Independent phases and4,000/4,001ps drift plus4,001/1,900ps ratio; multiple pointer wraps, complete upper bits/metadata, held pressure, either-domain reset, stopped-clock restart, loss and malformed length.
validation.limitations: Digital simulation cannot establish metastability MTBF, physical Gray-bus skew, clock-domain path constraints, synchronizer cell preservation or reset distribution. Native IHP mapping, structural CDC and post-layout checks remain pending.
validation.selected_case_scope: Ten single-case fault runs deliberately select one scenario (one actual failure plus six unselected entries); a separate successful selection regression checks exact name and count. All three full positive suites execute every case with zero skipped.
